test_policy.notes: ACT or SAT scores are not required for undergraduate international applicants (except athletes); submitting them can qualify students for academic scholarships.

requirements.notes: Own online application; $60 non-refundable fee. New freshmen need completion of secondary school with a cumulative GPA of 2.5 or better (converted to the US scale). Steps: apply, apply for scholarships, receive admission package, apply for visa. Essays and recommendations are not listed.

deadlines.label: International fall 2027 application deadline
deadlines.notes: Rolling admission; the cost page prints Fall: May 1 without a year (treated as 2027). Spring: Oct. 1; summer: March 1.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Proficiency is shown by citizenship of Australia, Belize, Canada (except Quebec), Commonwealth Caribbean, Ghana, Ireland, Liberia, New Zealand, Nigeria, UK or US; a degree completed in one of those countries; or four years of Cambridge International curriculum / two years of AS or A level. Scores below the exemption level do not necessarily block admission: students are tested at orientation and may receive an I-20 for the Intensive English Program (IEP) first. Scores may be submitted until the first day of international orientation.

english.notes: This is the exemption level from the ESU English placement test (academic I-20); no new 1-6 scale value is listed.

cost.notes: ESU international page (no academic year is printed; entered as 2026-2027 as the current page): non-resident undergraduate flat-rate tuition and fees $15,675 (12+ credit hours with at least one on campus), on-campus living $9,950, insurance/books/etc. $3,000 (entered as other), total $28,625. The page also lists a lower 'Partnership/Diversity Award' rate (tuition and fees $10,125, total $23,075) without stating who qualifies. Kansas resident total is $20,305.

aid.notes: Presidential Scholarship is automatic from the admission application and transcripts: $1,250-$3,000 per year by unweighted GPA (3.0 to 3.95+) or ACT (21 to 30+), renewable with a 3.0 ESU GPA and 24 credit hours. The international page says it is based on SAT and/or GPA. Also an International Ambassador Scholarship (leadership) and transfer scholarships (24+ credits). Stackable scholarships cannot exceed the cost of attendance. No international need-based aid is described.

sat.note: The international pages print no SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search. SAT/ACT are optional.

act.note: The international pages print no ACT code; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: No TOEFL institution code is printed; look it up in the ETS code search.
